design:
Validate "what users will say" (orchestrator 01:15Z Nov 12) against real Product Hunt launch comments.
Sample: launches Aug-Oct 2026 in the thread dumps (raw/ph_predict_data/comments) with >= 8 non-team comments (team = real
maker/poster handles); pilot N=30 then N=300 (SEED fixed). Product-only inputs: name, tagline, description, topics.
Steps (Gemini on Vertex, temperature 0, JSON; no Claude):
  PRED_PLAIN    the website's prompt (file passed in; placeholder until the site sends its exact prompt) -> 5 themes
  PRED_PERSONA  the same + "consider these user types" (the E5 role segments) -> 5 themes
  TRUTH         a separate call that sees only the real non-team comments (up to 40, 400 chars each) -> up to 8 themes,
                each with the number of comments raising it; never sees any prediction
  GENERIC       (baseline a) the 5 most central real themes of OTHER launches with the same first topic (embedding centrality)
  SHUFFLE       (baseline b) the PRED_PLAIN themes of a different random launch with the same first topic
  JUDGE         blinded: real theme list + one candidate list (labelled only "list B", order of candidates randomised per call)
                -> for each real theme, covered y/n; for each candidate theme, present in real comments y/n
  EMBED         gemini-embedding-001 cosine; a theme matches if cos >= 0.80 (also mean best-match cosine)
Metrics per launch: recall = share of real themes covered (weighted by comment count, and unweighted); precision = share of
candidate themes present. Means with launch-bootstrap 95% CIs; paired differences PRED - GENERIC and PRED - SHUFFLE,
PERSONA - PLAIN. The simulation counts only if PRED beats both baselines with intervals above zero.

truth: Users appreciate the ability to find information based on what they remember, not just exact keywords, and the value of their own context in the age of AI.
The difficulty of adding content and importing existing bookmarks into such systems is a major concern.
Users are asking about the ability to export saved content and whether the system remembers everything checked or only saved items.
Users are interested in seamless import of existing bookmarks and integration with email and chat platforms.
The visual design of the website, particularly the background art, is highly praised.
There is a question about how Ancher handles conflicting information from different saved sources.
The feature of finding the exact moment in a saved video with the source attached is highlighted as very useful.
The AI voice in the video mispronouncing 'Ancher' was noted as a minor issue.
pred_plain: The ability to turn everything I read and save into work I can ship, especially generating research briefs, reports, and presentations in my own voice, sounds incredibly powerful and time-saving.
I'm concerned about the privacy and security of my captured articles, videos, PDFs, and personal ideas, especially since AI is involved in processing them.
How does Ancher 2.0 handle duplicate content or conflicting information from various sources I capture?
It would be great if Ancher 2.0 could integrate directly with popular project management tools like Notion or Asana for seamless workflow integration.
How does Ancher 2.0 differentiate itself from existing AI note-taking and knowledge management tools like Mem.ai or Obsidian, especially regarding the 'work you can ship' aspect?
generic: Users are curious about how the product handles context across multiple tools and applications.
Users are curious about how well the product handles messy open-ended answers.
Users inquire about the product's functionality for non-developers and its applicability to diverse workflows.
Users want to know more about the functionality and adaptability of the 'Learn Anywhere' feature.
Users are curious about specific use cases and limitations, such as task locking, live search limits, and cost.
